name: Narragansett Bay and Block Island
blurb: Eelgrass, menhaden and shellfish feeding bass, ospreys and whales.

tip.title: Add more nitrogen
tip.text: Nitrogen feeds the bay's algae. Raise Nitrogen from land and sewage by 100% and follow the change through phytoplankton, menhaden and the predators that eat them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Light reaching shallow water and marsh drives growth of algae, eelgrass and marsh plants.

nodes.name: Bacteria and detritus feeders
nodes.desc: Break down dead marsh grass, eelgrass and algae, and release nutrients back into the water.
Drifting algae that form the base of the food chain for many of the bay's marine animals.
Underwater meadows that shelter young fish, give mussels a place to attach and feed geese and brant.
Salt-marsh grass of the tidal edge. Its dead stems feed the detritus-based part of the marsh food web.
Tiny drifting crustaceans that graze phytoplankton and are eaten by young menhaden and other small fish.
A schooling filter-feeding fish. Many predators, including striped bass, bluefish, osprey and dolphins, eat it.
Filter-feeding mollusc that clings to rocks, piers and eelgrass, eating plankton.
Grazes on grasses and, as shown in other bays, on eelgrass rhizomes.
Small grass-eating rodent of fields and dunes. GloBI records link it to seaside goldenrod.
An opportunistic predatory fish of the bay. Menhaden are a notable part of its diet.
A fast schooling predator that hunts menhaden and other forage fish along the coast.
A fish-eating raptor that nests around the bay; menhaden are among its prey.
A sea duck that winters on the coast and dives for mussels and other shellfish.
Abundant coastal gull that eats shellfish, fish and scavenged carrion.

nodes.name: Common bottlenose dolphin
nodes.desc: A toothed whale that eats schooling fish such as menhaden; recorded in waters off the bay.
A baleen whale that gulps schools of small fish; it is the most recorded mammal around the bay mouth in GBIF.
